title: Design System: Del trazo al volumen

display.purpose: The one headline per scene; balanced, max 16ch. A plain note and the stage name go under it.

headline.purpose: Exploded-view layer words as a column or as the narrow-screen caption (2.25rem).

label.purpose: Layer words hung off leader lines on wide screens.

shadows.name: point-of-light
shadows.value: 0 0 6px 1px color-mix(in oklab, #ede6da 80%, transparent), 0 0 28px 6px color-mix(in oklab, #ede6da 18%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Preloader point of light only; interface elements are otherwise flat.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Every CSS transition: decelerates like a load settling.

motion.name: duration-cursor
motion.purpose: Crosshair folding into the pick box.

motion.name: duration-button
motion.purpose: Button fill shift copper to bone.

motion.name: duration-callout
motion.purpose: Leader line and layer word reveal.

motion.name: duration-preloader
motion.purpose: Preloader fade into the WebGL point.

motion.name: scene-ease
motion.purpose: Scroll choreography of camera and uniforms; no overshoot. Reduced motion: finished building, only the sun moves.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Below it, exploded-view words become a single caption on a plumb line.

components.name: WhatsApp Button
components.description: The page's single action, in the closing scene.

components.name: Scene Sentence
components.description: One sentence per scene, at most one copper word.

components.name: Leader-line Callout
components.description: Exploded-view layer word hung off a hairline: the part name with its role under it, always shown dim; hover lengthens the line and lights the name copper.

components.css: .ds-callouts{display:grid;gap:1rem;padding:1.5rem;background:#141210;} .ds-callout{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:.9rem;font-family:'DM Sans',sans-serif;font-weight:500;font-size:clamp(.95rem,.85rem + .35vw,1.15rem);letter-spacing:.01em;color:#ede6da;cursor:pointer;} .ds-leader{display:block;width:clamp(1.75rem,4vw,3.5rem);height:1px;background:color-mix(in oklab,#ede6da 45%,transparent);transition:width .9s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1)),background-color .9s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1));} .ds-word{opacity:.6;transition:opacity .9s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1)),translate .9s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1)),color .9s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1));} .ds-callout:hover .ds-leader{width:clamp(3rem,7vw,6rem);background:var(--color-accent,#b8743a);} .ds-callout:hover .ds-word{opacity:1;translate:0 0;color:var(--color-accent,#b8743a);} .ds-word{display:grid;gap:0.2rem;} .ds-role{font-size:0.85em;font-weight:400;color:#ede6da;opacity:0.75;}

components.name: CAD Cursor
components.description: Copper crosshair replacing the pointer; folds into a square pick box over interactive targets.

components.name: Scroll Hint
components.description: Scene 1 button: the word "Bajar" over a thin arrow drifting down; a click or a tap takes the first step.
components.css: .ds-hint-wrap{display:grid;place-items:center;padding:1.5rem;background:#141210;} .ds-hint{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;gap:0.4rem;padding:0.5rem 1.25rem;border:0;background:none;color:#ede6da;font:500 0.9rem/1.2 "DM Sans",sans-serif;letter-spacing:0.01em;cursor:pointer;} .ds-hint-label{opacity:0.6;transition:opacity 0.6s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1));} .ds-hint:hover .ds-hint-label,.ds-hint:focus-visible .ds-hint-label{opacity:1;} .ds-hint-arrow{display:block;fill:none;stroke:currentColor;stroke-width:1;vector-effect:non-scaling-stroke;animation:ds-descend 3.2s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1)) infinite;} @keyframes ds-descend{0%{translate:0 -0.4rem;opacity:0}25%{opacity:0.8}75%{opacity:0.8}100%{translate:0 0.4rem;opacity:0}}

components.name: Point of Light
components.description: The preloader's breathing point, handed over to the WebGL scene.
components.css: .ds-pl{display:grid;place-items:center;height:6rem;background:#141210;} .ds-point{width:5px;height:5px;border-radius:50%;background:#ede6da;box-shadow:0 0 6px 1px color-mix(in oklab,#ede6da 80%,transparent),0 0 28px 6px color-mix(in oklab,#ede6da 18%,transparent);animation:ds-breathe 2.8s var(--ease-settle, cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1)) infinite alternate;} @keyframes ds-breathe{from{opacity:.55;scale:.85}to{opacity:1;scale:1}}

narrative.overview:
One continuous dark frame in which a building is drawn, raised, clad, lit, taken apart and shrunk to a model, all driven by the visitor's scroll. The page has no chrome: no nav, no logo, no cards, no grid of content. Each scene carries at most one sentence, set large in a serif and given air, while the 3D scene does the rest of the talking. Interface marks borrow from the drafting table: hairline leader lines like axonometric callouts, a drifting arrow under the word "Bajar" for the scroll hint, a CAD crosshair for the pointer.

Material character comes from architecture rather than from UI: board-formed concrete with formwork tie holes, warm wood, dark glass, hard raking light, and a balsa study model under one lamp. Everything is procedural; no image is downloaded. A fine concrete grain sits over the whole frame, scene included.

Motion is slow and heavy: every transition decelerates like a load settling, nothing bounces, there is no sound. Stopping the scroll leaves the stroke or the extrusion halfway. Under reduced motion the finished building stands still and only the light follows the scroll.
keyCharacteristics: Three interface colours (warm black, bone, copper) and two faces.
One headline per scene, display serif, at most one copper word in it; under it, a plain note on what the studio does in that stage and the stage name.
Hairline (1px) linework for every interface mark; no boxes, no radii.
Charcoal sketch strokes that overshoot corners, waver and thin at their ends.
A ground floor plan drafted to convention after the sketch (poché, door swings, windows, stair, axes, dimensions, room names with areas and levels, north point, scale); the building rises from it.
A single heavy easing curve for every CSS transition.

rules.name: The One Copper Word Rule
rules.body: A scene sentence carries at most one copper word, set through `<em>` (rendered upright, never italic). Copper appears elsewhere only on the cursor, the closing button and the active exploded-view layer.

rules.name: The Three Colours Rule
rules.body: The interface palette is base, bone and copper; Tailwind's default colours are cleared (`--color-*: initial`). Tints come from `color-mix` of bone, not from new hexes.

rules.name: The Sentence, Not a Heading Rule
rules.body: Display type is used for whole sentences, not for titles over content. There are no eyebrows, kickers or small caps above them: the stage name closes the block, under the note, lettered like the plan sheet title.

rules.name: The Upright Emphasis Rule
rules.body: `em` is never italic; emphasis is colour (copper) alone.

rules.name: The Depth Lives in the Scene Rule
rules.body: Interface elements never cast shadows; anything that needs depth is built in the 3D scene and lit.

dos: Do use the settle curve (`cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.61, 0.24, 1)`) for every CSS transition, with durations between 0.4s and 1.2s.
Do keep scene choreography on `power1`/`power2` in-out curves with scrub smoothing; nothing overshoots.
Do draw every interface mark as a 1px line in bone or copper.
Do keep one headline per scene, display serif, with at most one copper word; the note and the stage name go under it, never above.
Do generate textures procedurally (formwork panels and tie holes, wood grain, the SVG grain overlay at 9% soft-light).
Do give reduced motion the finished building, with only the light following the scroll.
donts: Don't add colours beyond base, bone and copper to the interface; derive tints with `color-mix` of bone.
Don't round corners or add box shadows to interface elements.
Don't use bounce, spring, or overshoot easing, and don't add sound.
Don't italicise emphasis; copper is the emphasis.
Don't put a nav, logo or second action on the page; the single action arrives in the last scene.
Don't render the building as a clean CAD wireframe; strokes overshoot, waver and thin like charcoal. The sketch is charcoal; the plan that follows it is not.

Don't draw the plan as a diagram of boxes: an architect reads it, so it carries poché, door swings, window symbols, the stair, axes, dimensions, room names with areas and levels, the north point and a scale.
